title: Entitlement ledger: scope contracts and admin-safety lattice
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design an "entitlement ledger" for RBAC v2 that formalizes scope contracts between resources and roles, supports multi-tenant resource hierarchies, enables strong audit logging, and integrates SSO/SAML group assertions into safe admin controls. Goals: (1) Define a compact, versionable permissions matrix that maps roles -> scope contracts -> allowed actions; (2) Model resource hierarchy (global -> organization -> project -> deployment -> model) with inheritance/override rules and explicit deny; (3) Provide an append-only entitlement ledger for change history and auditability; (4) Define SSO/SAML assertion mappings and bootstrap flows for group->role bindings; (5) Define admin-safety lattice (breakglass, temporal elevation, canary rollouts for admin changes); (6) Minimize runtime lookup cost for high-throughput inference paths while preserving explainability for incidents.

Constraints: must interoperate with Dedicated and Private deployments (local KMS, no central control plane guarantees), and must work with existing console rollout UI and Optimize heuristics.

Proposed data model (high level):
- Entitlement ledger entries (immutable): {actor, action, resource_path, scope_contract_id, change_type, reason, timestamp, performed_by}
- Scope contract: a small policy blob containing allowed_actions (list), resource_selector (prefix), inheritance_policy (inherit | isolate), expiry (optional), source (SSO | UI | API), version_id
- Role binding: principal -> scope_contract_id (+conditions)
- Permission matrix: canonical set of atomic actions (e.g., inference:invoke, model:promote, infra:scale) combined via allow/deny/temporal rules

Decisions so far: prefer prefix-based resource_selector (fast lookup) over full graph resolution to keep constant-time checks; ledger is append-only (no soft deletes) with snapshot checkpoints for fast lookups.

Trade-offs: prefix selectors are simpler & performant but less expressive for complex graph cross-tenancy rules; we'll mitigate by allowing explicit deny and scoped role isolation.

Migration strategy: create an adapter to read existing rolegraph and emit initial ledger with scope_contracts mapping and a short audit window where both legacy and new checks run (shadow mode).

Compatibility: runtime should consult local snapshot of ledger + cache for hot prefixes to meet latency SLOs; changes commit to ledger and trigger async checkpoint and pub/sub notification for runtimes to refresh.

Audit requirements:
- All changes must include actor, justification (free text limited to 512 chars), approver (if from UI and >P2 change), and optional ticket link.
- Queryable by time range, actor, resource prefix, and change_type.
- Retain raw ledger for 7 years (configurable per customer for Private).

SSO/SAML mapping:
- Support group->scope_contract binding with precedence rules: explicit user binding > group binding > default role.
- Support attribute-based matching (SAMLP attribute urn:redwood:roleHint) to suggest scope contracts at first login.
- Must include an onboarding flow in Console for admins to approve suggested bindings before applying.

Admin controls & safety lattice:
- Breakglass: time-limited elevation with multi-factor approval and audit binding.
- Canary admin rollouts: staged assignment of high-priv roles to a subset of tenants to observe side effects.
- Safe revoke: revoke propagates but still logs access checks that occurred in last 24h for incident review.

Open questions:
- TTL/expiry semantics for temporary scope contracts (policy vs. enforcement in runtime)?
- Fine-grained deny strategy when multiple scope_contracts apply; prefer explicit deny priority but need deterministic resolution algorithm.
- How much of the ledger indexing will be stored in the control plane vs. pushed to Private deployments?

Next steps: document schema, implement ledger append API, design Console onboarding UX, and draft runtime adapter + migration plan.
